summary_html: Federal **Child and Family Services Reviews (CFSR)** monitor state performance on safety, permanency, and well-being. Project Milk Carton flags states that repeatedly fail or never publish CFSR improvement plans.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that the department must make reasonable efforts to reunify before seeking termination, that a judge may weigh a failure of those efforts in deciding whether unfitness is merely temporary, but that a reasonable-efforts failure does not preclude an order in the child's best interest; it affirmed termination and left future visitation to the adoptive parents.
key_cases.relevance: The reasonable-efforts finding is the judicial determination on which federal Title IV-E eligibility and CFSR performance measurement depend.
key_cases.quote: Before seeking to terminate parental rights, the department must make “reasonable efforts” aimed at restoring the child to the care of the natural parents.

key_cases.holding: The SJC held that although impounded care and protection records carry a strong statutory privacy interest, a journalist showed good cause under Rule 7 of the Uniform Rules on Impoundment Procedure for release of audio recordings of hearings in the case of a child who was placed with her father without a completed ICPC home study and later went missing and died, and the judge abused her discretion in refusing release.
key_cases.relevance: Adele shows the SJC weighing public accountability for departmental performance against the confidentiality that ordinarily shields that performance from review.
key_cases.quote: a person seeking access to impounded materials in a care and protection proceeding faces a high hurdle

key_cases.holding: The Appeals Court affirmed a temporary custody order, holding that social worker affidavits filed with the petition are not categorically inadmissible at the seventy-two hour hearing but are admissible only to the extent permitted by Adoption of Luc, that unpreserved hearsay objections are waived, and that the judge did not deny the father due process by intermittently muting his participation in a remote hearing.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion illustrates the judicial checks Massachusetts applies at the earliest stage of agency custody, the stage federal reviews measure for timeliness and quality.
key_cases.quote: The judge acted within her discretion, and within constitutional bounds, in intermittently limiting the father's participation at the hearing, which took place through an Internet-based video conferencing platform.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed, holding that the "reasonable efforts" clause of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act of 1980 confers no federally enforceable right on the children it benefits and creates no implied private cause of action, leaving compliance to be enforced by the Secretary of Health and Human Services through the state-plan approval and funding process.
key_cases.relevance: Suter explains why CFSR-style federal review by HHS, rather than private litigation, is the mechanism that polices a State's Title IV-E performance.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.
